# Hard rules for coding agents

No exceptions without the owner's explicit say.

- **Ask, don't guess.** If the task is unclear or the spec looks wrong,
  ask before building. Pushing back on a wrong spec is part of the job.
- **Smallest footprint.** Change only what the task needs. No drive-by
  refactors, no unrequested files, layers, dependencies or options.
- **Goal-focused.** Every changed line serves the stated problem.
  Anything else goes to the backlog, not into the diff.
- **Simplest proper solution.** Solve the real problem the simplest way
  that is professionally sound. No workarounds, hacks, suppressed errors,
  special cases to make a test pass, or "temporary" fixes. If the proper
  fix is out of reach, stop and say why instead of working around it.
- **Clean and solid.** Clear names. Match the surrounding style. Fix the
  root cause, not the symptom.
- **No stale code, no duplication.** Remove what your change makes stale:
  dead code, unused imports, functions, flags, files, outdated comments
  and docs. No commented-out code and no legacy copies "just in case":
  git keeps the history. Where your change touches duplicated logic,
  merge it into one source. Duplication elsewhere goes to the backlog.
- **Reuse first.** Before implementing anything, search the repo for an
  existing component, helper or pattern that does the job. Use or extend
  it. Build new only when nothing fits, and build it reusable.
- **Lean work.** Delete before you add. Touch as few files as the fix
  allows.
- **Prove it works.** Run the repo's lint, type-check and tests before
  saying "done". Report failures as they are, never as passing.
- **Safe by default.** No secrets in code, logs or commits. No destructive
  action without the owner's OK: force push, history rewrite on a shared
  branch, deleting data, migrations against production.
- **A history people can read.** One commit per logical change, not per
  step. Fold fix-ups ("fix typo", "wip", "address review") into the
  commit they fix before pushing; after pushing, add a normal commit.
  Messages say what and why: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>`. Each feature
  lands as one squash commit, through a pull request or a local
  `git merge --squash`. A promotion (`staging` → `main`) is a merge
  commit, never a squash. The repo's branch model:
  `.claude/rules/project.md`.
- **Plain speech.** Short sentences. Simple words. Say what changed and
  why, nothing more. Applies to chat, commits, PRs and comments.

*Enforcement:* the pre-commit hook runs the checks; squash merging is enabled
and used for feature pull requests (a GitHub setting). `/second-review`
flags any change the task did not need,
any workaround where a proper fix exists, stale code left behind, and any
code that duplicates an existing component. Compliance is
review-only.

# Coding Principles

Binding for human and AI contributors. Numbers match the long form in
brain-os (profiles/ai-factory/evidence.md). Stack specifics (schema
library, backlog, CI, branch model) are named in
`.claude/rules/project.md`. More principles load with the files they apply
to: `.claude/rules/brain-os/boundaries.md`,
`.claude/rules/brain-os/data.md`, `.claude/rules/brain-os/tests.md`.

- **(1) Deep modules, shallow surface.** Few modules with strong interfaces.
  Split only at a real deployment or testability boundary, never for
  line count. *Why:* over-fragmented code is harder for people and
  models to follow. *Mechanism:* review asks "how many files would the
  next change to this concept touch?" (review-only)
- **(3) Every rule ships with a mechanism.** A rule with no hook, lint rule,
  CI check or test is a suggestion. *Why:* prose-only rules quietly stop
  being followed. *Mechanism:* a new rule names its mechanism, or goes
  to the backlog marked `(unenforced)`.
- **(4) Verify, don't self-trust.** Nobody reviews their own diff and calls
  it done. Changes to auth, access control, payments or migrations get a
  fresh-context second review before merge. *Why:* green gates are not a
  correctness proof. *Mechanism:* branch protection with review and green
  CI; `/second-review` for agent-authored changes.
- **(6) Gates are honestly labeled.** A step that cannot fail is never
  marked blocking. One that should not block yet is advisory, with a
  plan to promote it. *Why:* a fake gate is worse than none.
  *Mechanism:* each CI step declares blocking or advisory next to it.
- **(7) AI output is an amplifier, not a shortcut.** Fix typing, error
  handling and tests before scaling agent-written volume. Budget a
  whole-surface review that no single phase owns. *Why:* agent-written
  code carries more defects on a weak base. (review-only)
- **(8) Names are compressed documentation.** A clear name beats a comment
  explaining a vague one. *Why:* people and models both read names as
  meaning. *Mechanism:* code review.
- **Docs change with behaviour.** README, changelog and comments are
  updated in the same change as the code they describe. Comments say
  why, not what. *Mechanism:* review.

Evidence and long form: brain-os, profiles/ai-factory/evidence.md.

# Project: bookete-os

Internal tools for bookete's sales work: finding restaurants in Austria and
working them as leads. Two parts, each with its own `package.json`:

- `src/`, `test/`: the lead scraper. Node ESM CLI, no dependencies.
  OpenStreetMap discovery plus competitor-widget detection, CSV out.
- `crm/`: the bookete CRM at crm.bookete.com, for two users and their agents.
  Cloudflare Worker + D1 + static assets. Google Workspace sign-in, Gmail
  sending, a remote MCP server for agents.

## Commands

- Scraper tests: `npm test`
- CRM tests: `npm --prefix crm test`
- CRM build (web bundle): `npm --prefix crm run build`
- CRM local run: `cd crm && npm run dev` (needs `crm/.dev.vars`, see `crm/README.md`)
- `AGENTS.md` is generated: `python3 .claude/agents_md.py .` after changing `.claude/rules/`

## CRM architecture

- `crm/src/domain/`: pure business rules (lead fields, statuses, follow-up
  cadence, opt-out). Shared by server and browser.
- `crm/src/application/use-cases.js`: the only write path. The web app,
  MCP and backup import all call it, so every rule holds whoever writes.
  Import adds only records the CRM never held, through the same normalization.
- Concurrent writes: a write computed from a read names that read as `base`;
  the store commits it only if the record is unchanged (`write_guard`,
  migration 0002), else the use case runs again on fresh data after a short
  random wait (`retrying`, `retryPause`).
  The store refuses a patch, remove or restore without a `base`; only a put
  (a new record, or the ICP) goes without.
  History rows come from triggers on `docs`, so no write path can skip them.
- `crm/src/server/`: Worker entry (`index.js`), D1 document store, Google
  sign-in and sessions (`auth.js`), Gmail, RPC commands, MCP.
- `crm/src/web/`: the browser UI, bundled by esbuild to `crm/public/app.js`.
- Access: `allowedUser()` in `crm/src/server/auth.js` is the one check.
  Web sessions and MCP tokens both end there; `ALLOWED_EMAILS` decides.
  The one route that touches lead data without a session is the
  unsubscribe link (`/abmelden/`, `crm/src/server/unsubscribe.js`, routed
  in `index.js`): its HMAC decides, and it can only opt out the lead it was
  made for.
- Agents may draft email, never send it. Sending is a person in the web app.

## Stack specifics the rules refer to

- Schema library (principle 2): Zod 4, at every request and env boundary
  (`crm/src/server/commands.js`, `mcp.js`, `config.js`).
- Migrations: `crm/migrations/`, applied by `wrangler d1 migrations apply`.
- D1 test double: `crm/test/d1.js` runs on node:sqlite and refuses more than
  100 bound parameters per query, as D1 does. D1's cap on queries per Worker
  invocation (50 on Free) is not modelled (unenforced; backlog).
- Backlog: `docs/backlog.md`, groomed with `/groom-backlog` at each CRM release.
- Release: each production deploy bumps `version` in `crm/package.json` and adds a `crm/CHANGELOG.md` entry.
- Access walk: `crm/test/access.test.js` calls every API route and RPC command without a valid session. A new command goes into its exact list.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Deploy runs only after tests pass on `main`.
- Branch model: stage `early`. Feature branch → `main`, one squash commit per feature.

# Rules for specific files

- Before you change files matching `**/api/**`, `**/actions/**`, `**/actions.*`, `**/server/**`, `**/auth/**`, `**/middleware.*`, `**/webhooks/**`, `**/cron/**`, `**/functions/**`, read `.claude/rules/brain-os/boundaries.md`.
- Before you change files matching `**/migrations/**`, `**/*.sql`, `**/schema.*`, `**/schema/**`, `**/db/**`, `supabase/**`, `prisma/**`, `drizzle/**`, read `.claude/rules/brain-os/data.md`.
- Before you change files matching `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**`, `tests/**`, `test/**`, `e2e/**`, read `.claude/rules/brain-os/tests.md`.
